intro.description: A real-time electromagnetic instrument that resolves magnetic vectors, electric-field activity, RF peaks, and system confidence.

opening.title: Electromagnetic interference is unwanted electromagnetic energy that flows into other systems.
opening.tagline: It leaks from motors, chargers, radios and wiring, rides along cables and through the air, and disturbs whatever it reaches. Inductra Vaion measures it as magnetic, electric and radio-frequency energy, so you can see where it comes from and how strong it is.

hero.title: Inductra Vaion
hero.description: A real-time electromagnetic diagnostic instrument built on a Raspberry Pi. It reads a [[QMC5883P three-axis magnetometer]] and an [[ADS1115 electric-field probe]] over [[I²C]], sweeps [[100 kHz to 6 GHz]] with a [[tinySA Ultra]] over USB, resolves the field into [[magnetic vectors]], [[relative E-field activity]] and [[tracked RF peaks]], and adds fine-resolution complex-IQ capture through an [[RTL-SDR]] — translating invisible electromagnetic behaviour into a human sixth sense.

globe.label: Interactive Earth with selectable electromagnetic research nodes

nodes.name: USA · NIST
nodes.summary: Developed the calculable standard-field methods — TEM cells and calculable dipole antennas — that let an electric-field probe be read in volts per metre.

nodes.name: CANADA · NRC
nodes.summary: Developed Canada’s primary electrical standards, including the Josephson voltage reference every calibrated voltmeter is traced back to.

nodes.name: UNITED KINGDOM · NPL
nodes.summary: Built the first caesium atomic clock here in 1955, and developed the RF and microwave power standards used for field-strength work.

nodes.name: GERMANY · PTB
nodes.summary: Developed and maintains the quantum Hall resistance standard that realises the ohm, and the magnetic-flux-density standards used to calibrate magnetometers.

nodes.name: FRANCE · LNE
nodes.summary: Developed the calculable capacitor chain that fixes the farad, and France’s reference antennas for radiated field strength.

nodes.name: JAPAN · NMIJ/AIST
nodes.summary: Developed the antenna-factor calibration methods used across Asia to turn an antenna voltage into a stated field strength.

nodes.name: SOUTH KOREA · KRISS
nodes.summary: Developed near-field probe calibration and RF power standards, and the atomic magnetometer work behind low-field sensing.

nodes.name: INDIA · CSIR–NPL
nodes.summary: Developed India’s national electrical and radio-frequency standards, and the EMI/EMC test capability the region certifies against.

nodes.name: AUSTRALIA · NMIA
nodes.summary: Developed Australia’s RF and microwave calibration chain, including the power and attenuation references used for field measurement.

nodes.name: BRAZIL · INMETRO
nodes.summary: Developed Brazil’s electrical metrology chain and the EMC conformity testing South America certifies equipment against.

nodes.name: SOUTH AFRICA · CSIR
nodes.summary: Developed South Africa’s antenna, radar and electromagnetic sensing research — the national capability nearest to this instrument.

pages.label: Sixth Sense
pages.title: What the trusted channels mean together.
pages.copy: MTDI asks whether the measurements are trustworthy; Sixth Sense explains what the trusted channels mean together.

sections.title: Learn, lock, compare
sections.copy: Each channel learns a reference in a quiet environment, then that reference is frozen. These never adapt on their own — you ask for a new one explicitly.

sections.title: A score that can be taken apart
sections.copy: MTDI is a weighted index over eight named factors — availability, baseline, signal-to-noise, clipping, timing, transient behaviour, axial consensus and correlation. The weights are visible, the factors are listed, and the confidence is computed from measurable quantities rather than typed in.

sections.title: Nothing claimed beyond the evidence
sections.copy: Detection limits are derived from each channel’s own measured noise ([[LOD = 3σ]], [[LOQ = 10σ]]). Repeatability is a real repeated measurement, reported as an RSD with a Student’s t 95 % interval.

sections.title: Two independent implementations
sections.copy: Everything the Python engine computes is recomputed from the same recorded samples by an independent MATLAB toolbox. Two implementations agreeing on one capture is the reason to believe either.

sections.title: D4 analysis engine
sections.copy: D4 asks what the field is doing: robust z-scores, cross-sensor consensus, mains harmonics and THD at the ADC’s real sample rate, RF sweep analysis and transient characterisation.
